llm.summary: This is a disclosed, read-only VMware log-query skill, with the main cautions being local password handling and trust in the externally installed package.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs network access to the configured Log Insight appliance and credentials for authenticated reads; that is proportionate to querying enterprise logs, which may still contain sensitive operational data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned uv/PyPI package and an optional uvx MCP launch path; this is disclosed and common for a CLI-backed skill, but the executable implementation and package hashes are not included in the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to VMware/vSphere/ESXi log investigation, include routing away from unrelated VMware tasks, require bounded log searches, and explicitly treat log text as untrusted data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates persistent local config, may store a password in ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env, rewrites plaintext to reversible b64 obfuscation, and writes audit records to ~/.vmware/audit.db; these behaviors are disclosed and not hidden persistence mechanisms.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is VMware Log Insight search, aggregation, metadata, and alert-history lookup, and the documented tool surface is limited to seven read-only operations with no ingest, create, edit, or delete capability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable trusting the pinned external vmware-log-insight package and the linked source. Use a dedicated read-only Log Insight service account, keep TLS verification enabled except for controlled lab appliances, prefer secret-manager or process-level environment injection over storing passwords in .env, and protect any local .env and audit database files because logs and credentials can be sensitive.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The --skip-auth flag is documented only for the doctor diagnostic command, not for normal log queries or MCP operation, so it does not show tool-parameter abuse in the artifact.
[PE3] expected: The skill uses a per-target password to authenticate to Log Insight and documents .env storage, chmod 600, and secret-manager injection; credential use is purpose-aligned, though users should prefer non-persistent secret injection when possible.
[RA2] expected: The matched paths describe installation/config files and an audit database, not cron jobs, services, startup hooks, or autonomous background persistence.
[TM3] expected: TLS verification is on by default, and --skip-auth is limited to diagnostics; the artifact does not show unsafe defaults for normal operation.
[PE2] expected: chmod 600 is a restrictive file-permission command and does not require sudo or root privileges; it is appropriate for the documented password file.
[T08] expected: The externally resolved vmware-log-insight package is a real supply-chain trust boundary because the implementation is not vendored or hash-pinned in the artifact, but this is disclosed and not evidence of malicious behavior.
[T09] expected: The reversible b64 password rewrite is accurately described as obfuscation, not encryption, and the docs recommend secret-manager injection for real at-rest secrecy.
